Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was about the DRC, not Congo Republic (COG) — wrong country. ITU DataHub records 77.5% 4G population coverage for Congo (Rep.) in 2024, and GSMA's June 2026 report on the Republic of Congo cites 86–89% 4G coverage. Both corroborate the 75-89% band. Revised from 3 to 4.

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source (data.worldbank.org/country/congo-dem-rep) was for DR Congo, not Congo Republic — wrong country. Corrected ITU/UN data show Congo Republic individuals-using-internet at 36.2% (2022) and DataReportal/Kepios put it at 38.4% (end 2025), both confirming the 30-49% band. Code confirmed unchanged.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was about the DRC, not Congo Republic — wrong country. Correct-country data show very high mobile connectivity (ARPCE regulator: 94.6% subscription penetration, 2023; GSMA/DataReportal: 93-99.8% connections, 2024-2026), but these are SIM/connection-based figures, not the unique-subscriber metric the scale requires, and no GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber percentage specific to Congo could be verified. Code tentatively retained at 4 given the strength of the connection-penetration data, but flagged for human review to confirm against GSMA's unique-subscriber dataset.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Value Name: Basic policy exists but limited implementation
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was a GOGLA brief for DRC, not Congo Republic — wrong country. Verified Congo-specific evidence shows an active National Energy Compact (2025-2030), a dedicated rural electrification agency (ANER), an EU-funded GET.transform programme developing mini-grid regulation, and on-the-ground pilots (UNDP micro-hydropower studies, Africa Solaire mini-grid). This is an active policy framework with some deployment, not merely a basic policy. Revised from 2 to 3.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was a document about the DRC (whose generation mix is ~97% hydro) wrongly cited for Congo Republic, which relies heavily on gas-fired thermal power. World Bank/IEA data (via CEIC) show Congo Republic's renewable electricity share at 26.3% (2021, down from 28.1% in 2020), with hydro alone at 35.0% in 2023 — solidly within the 25-49% band, not 75%+. Revised from 5 to 3.

Comments: Large gap women 75% less internet use

The only figure available is the Sub-Saharan Africa regional average (29% gap, 2025), which is not sufficiently country-specific to score confidently.
